findings.summary: Canonical READY can ignore modified tracked files hidden by Git index flags. Both assume-unchanged and skip-worktree concealed governance/control changes from status and ls-files --others while --require-ready returned READY.
Ordinary staged, unstaged, untracked and ignored files are now rejected by canonical READY validation.
Committed mode-120000 external metadata symlinks and mode-100755 control files are rejected; allowed READY paths must be in-repository regular 100644 blobs.

A legitimate synthetic READY/ACCEPT descendant passes, while out-of-scope changes, reviewed-content rename/deletion, unrelated ancestry, frozen request/schema/history drift, lifecycle contradictions, duplicate review IDs and acceptance-binding drift fail closed.
Capability prohibitions, nonempty primary/alternative temporal sets and non-temporal valid_time preservation remain enforced.

commands: verify remote PR head, commit, tree and reviewed-content digest
construct legitimate synthetic READY/ACCEPT descendant and run canonical --require-ready
dirty-state probes for staged, unstaged, untracked and ignored paths
mode-120000 external symlink and mode-100755 control-file probes
assume-unchanged and skip-worktree governance/control mutation probes
retest committed allowlist, ancestry, frozen controls, lifecycle, duplicate IDs and acceptance binding
conclusion: Round 8 closes ordinary dirty-worktree and symlink attacks, but index visibility flags can still conceal unreviewed tracked bytes. Validator-integrity remains CHANGES_REQUIRED.
